_note: Every 'at', 'crop' and 'highlight' coordinate is in RAW capture pixels, so
it can be checked by opening the file in screenshots/raw and reading the
point off directly. The CarPlay captures are 1920x720; the phone capture is
1320x2868. The Range tile occupies x 1611-1801, y 124-313 of the dashboard
capture — measured, not estimated (a luminance scan for the dark tile runs
against a backdrop of ~139 mean luminance versus ~65 inside a tile).

images.name: dashboard-where
images.caption: The Range & Efficiency tile on the CarPlay dashboard — top right in this layout.

images.name: range-tile
images.caption: Everything the tile is telling you. The trend line carries no numbers and no fixed scale on purpose — it is a shape to glance at, and the figure above it is the value.

callouts.label: Range remaining
callouts.detail: How far the app expects you to get on the energy left in the pack, at the pace you have been driving.

callouts.label: Efficiency right now
callouts.detail: Your efficiency over roughly the last few miles, in whichever unit you chose in Settings.

callouts.label: Green: better than your average
callouts.detail: The trend line covers about the last fifteen minutes. Green marks the stretches where you were doing better than your own recent average, amber where you were doing worse.

callouts.label: The dashed line is that average
callouts.detail: Your own average across what is shown — not a factory figure and not your lifetime average. It drifts as the window moves.

callouts.label: The dot is right now
callouts.detail: Amber here, so at this instant you were fractionally worse than your recent average — while still returning a perfectly healthy 3.4 mi/kWh.

images.name: arrival-soc
images.caption: Estimated arrival state of charge, during active navigation. Captured one minute after the tile above — the same drive, and the same 3.4 mi/kWh.

callouts.label: What you will arrive with
callouts.detail: How much charge the app expects to be left in the pack when you reach the destination.

callouts.label: Projected from this efficiency
callouts.detail: The same near-term figure the Range tile shows. Arrival SoC is that pace carried forward over the distance still to go.

callouts.label: Over this remaining distance
callouts.detail: 2.8 miles left here. The shorter the remaining distance, the less room the estimate has to be wrong.

images.name: drive-summary
images.caption: A finished drive in History. The displayed distance and energy are each rounded for display: 4.0 mi divided by 1.0 kWh looks like 4.0 mi/kWh, but the efficiency is computed from the unrounded pair and reads 3.9.

callouts.label: Efficiency for the whole drive
callouts.detail: Worked out once the drive ends, from its total distance and total energy — not an average of what the tile was showing along the way.

callouts.label: What the drive cost
callouts.detail: State of charge at the start and at the end. On a drive this short the percentage is coarse; the energy figure below is what the efficiency actually uses.

callouts.label: Distance measured by the app
callouts.detail: From GPS and the vehicle's own speed signal together, so a tunnel or a parking garage does not lose the miles.

callouts.label: Energy read from the pack
callouts.detail: The battery's own account of how much usable energy it has left, taken at the start and the end. Regeneration is netted off automatically.
